tasks.title: Implement gxstart — Linear intake and worktree creation
tasks.description: Create ~/.dotfiles/.scripts/gxstart. The script accepts a Linear ticket URL or ticket ID as its sole argument. It sources ~/.dotfiles/local/secrets.env to load LINEAR_API_KEY, then makes a single read-only curl call to Linear's GraphQL API to fetch the ticket's title, type (Bug→fix, Feature→feat, Spike→spike, else feat), and identifier (KEY-NUMBER). It generates a branch name in the format <prefix>/KEY-NUMBER-slug (slug derived from the ticket title, lowercased, spaces→hyphens, max 50 chars total). It calls the existing wt engine to create a worktree at ~/Documents/dev/worktrees/<repo-name>/<branch-name>/. It writes .worktree-meta.json into the worktree root with fields: linear_ticket_id, linear_url, ticket_title, branch_name, status ("picked"), picked_at (ISO 8601). Finally it adds .worktree-meta.json to ~/.gitignore_global if not already present. Errors: missing LINEAR_API_KEY → print 'LINEAR_API_KEY not set — source ~/.dotfiles/local/secrets.env' and exit 1. Missing arg → print usage and exit 1. Linear API HTTP error → print response and exit 1.
acceptance_criteria: Running gxstart with a Linear URL creates a worktree at ~/Documents/dev/worktrees/<repo>/<branch>/
Running gxstart with a ticket ID (e.g. KEY-123) also creates a worktree correctly
Branch name format is <prefix>/KEY-NUMBER-slug matching the Linear ticket type
.worktree-meta.json exists in the new worktree root with all six required fields
status field in .worktree-meta.json is 'picked' on creation
.worktree-meta.json is present in ~/.gitignore_global after first run
Missing LINEAR_API_KEY exits 1 with a descriptive error
Tests mock the curl call with a fixture JSON response and assert branch name and meta fields

tasks.title: Implement gxlist — worktree inventory dashboard
tasks.description: Create ~/.dotfiles/.scripts/gxlist. Default mode: scans ~/Documents/dev/worktrees/<current-repo-name>/ for subdirectories, reads .worktree-meta.json from each, and auto-detects building state by running 'git log origin/<base>..HEAD --oneline' inside the worktree — any local commits ahead of base means building (overrides meta status of 'picked'). Output is grouped into three sections: READY, BUILDING, PICKED. Each line shows: ticket title, branch name, and a clickable Linear URL (OSC 8 hyperlink if the terminal supports it, plain URL otherwise). --all flag: scans all repos under ~/Documents/dev/worktrees/. Worktrees with missing or malformed .worktree-meta.json are skipped with a stderr warning. Empty inventory prints 'No active worktrees.' and exits 0.
acceptance_criteria: Default mode shows only worktrees for the current repo (by dirname match)
--all flag shows worktrees across all repos in ~/Documents/dev/worktrees/
A worktree with local commits ahead of base is shown under BUILDING even if meta status is 'picked'
Output groups entries under READY, BUILDING, PICKED headings
Each entry includes the Linear URL
Malformed or missing .worktree-meta.json produces a stderr warning and is skipped
Tests use fixture worktree directories with pre-written .worktree-meta.json files and mock git log output

tasks.title: Implement gxship — rebase and ship a pre-built worktree
tasks.description: Create ~/.dotfiles/.scripts/gxship. The script must be run from inside a pre-built worktree (it reads .worktree-meta.json from CWD; exits 1 with a message if not found). Before prompting, it prints a descriptive message: 'Will rebase onto <base>, push to GitHub, create a PR, and trigger Linear to move the ticket to In Progress via auto-link.' Prompt varies by current meta status: if 'building' → 'Ship? [Y/n] -- Ready but later? [r]'; if 'ready' → 'Ship? [Y/n]'. Pressing Enter or Y → ship path: git fetch origin, git rebase origin/<base> (stops on conflict with message 'Conflict — resolve then re-run gxship', exit 1), updates meta status to 'shipped', calls ~/.dotfiles/.scripts/gxpush --auto --pr. Typing 'r' → updates meta status to 'ready', prints 'Marked as ready. Run gxship when you want to ship.', exits 0. Typing 'n' → aborts, exits 0. Script does not write back to Linear at any point.
acceptance_criteria: Running gxship outside a worktree (no .worktree-meta.json in CWD) exits 1 with a clear error
Descriptive pre-prompt message is printed before any confirmation
Building-state prompt includes the [r] option; ready-state prompt does not
'r' input sets meta status to 'ready' and exits 0 without pushing
Y/enter input triggers fetch, rebase, meta update to 'shipped', and gxpush --auto --pr
Rebase conflict causes exit 1 with a message directing the user to resolve and re-run
'n' input aborts cleanly with no changes
Tests mock gxpush and assert state transitions and prompt routing

tasks.title: Extend gxclean with --full cleanup flag
tasks.description: Extend ~/.dotfiles/.scripts/gxclean with a --full flag. Before any restructuring, write characterization tests that capture the current behavior: list of merged local branches, prompt, and deletion loop. Then add --full: Pass 1 — run 'git worktree list --porcelain' to find all registered worktrees, for each check if its branch is merged into origin/<base>; for each hit print the worktree path and branch, prompt 'Remove? [Y/n]', and on Y run 'wt rm <path>'. Pass 2 — run 'git fetch --prune origin', list remote-tracking branches with no local counterpart (via git branch -r | grep -v HEAD | grep -v 'origin/<base>'), prompt 'Prune remote <branch>? [Y/n]' for each, and on Y run 'git push origin --delete <branch>'. The existing behavior (no flag) is unchanged. Both passes run sequentially after the existing merged-local-branch pass when --full is supplied.
acceptance_criteria: Characterization tests exist and pass before any code changes (existing behavior coverage)
Running gxclean with no flags behaves identically to the current implementation
Running gxclean --full runs both new passes after the existing merged-branch cleanup
Pass 1 correctly identifies worktrees whose branch is merged and prompts per worktree
Pass 2 lists and prompts for stale remote-tracking branches
Declining any prompt (n) skips that item only — other items still proceed
Tests for --full mock wt rm and git push origin --delete and assert correct invocations

tasks.title: Evolve find-work skill to wrap gxlist
tasks.description: Update ~/.dotfiles/claude-code-shared/skills/find-work/SKILL.md and scripts/find-work.sh to delegate to gxlist instead of independently scanning branches. The skill becomes a thin wrapper: SKILL.md instructs the model to invoke the shell script, which in turn shells out to ~/.dotfiles/.scripts/gxlist (forwarding any --all flag if present). This mirrors the pattern used by the worktree skill wrapping the wt engine. The skill's behavior from the user's perspective is unchanged: invoking /find-work lists active work, now powered by the richer gxlist inventory (including state grouping and Linear URLs). Remove any branch-scanning logic previously in find-work.sh now covered by gxlist.
acceptance_criteria: find-work.sh delegates to ~/.dotfiles/.scripts/gxlist and forwards --all when provided
No duplicate branch-scanning logic remains in find-work.sh after the refactor
SKILL.md updated to reference gxlist as the underlying engine
The skill still runs correctly when invoked as /find-work in a Claude Code session
Tests verify that find-work.sh invokes gxlist with the correct arguments

follow_ups.title: Add LINEAR_API_KEY to ~/.dotfiles/local/secrets.env
steps: In Linear: click your avatar (bottom-left) > Settings > API > Personal API keys > Create key — name it 'gxstart', copy the token (starts with lin_api_)
Reload in every active shell: source ~/.dotfiles/local/secrets.env
Verify: echo $LINEAR_API_KEY — should print the token, not an empty string
